message.content:
The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) diverged from a common ancestor that is far back in mammalian history.  
- **Lion** → Family Felidae → Order Carnivora  
- **Zebra** → Family Equidae → Order Perissodactyla  

The most recent common ancestor of these two species is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. Both orders belong to the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, so the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. This ancestor lived roughly 90–100 million years ago, long before the split that produced the modern families of cats and horses.
